rationale: Slide B shows features weakly linked to KRAS mutation in the literature: abundant intracellular goblet-cell mucin, a villous or tubulovillous exophytic architecture, and an adenoma-like low-grade appearance. Slide A is a poorly differentiated, markedly pleomorphic, mucin-poor tumour with eosinophilic cytoplasm and solid/trabecular growth, which does not point either way, or slightly away, under these priors. The difference in mucin and villous growth is clear, but these are population-level tendencies with small effect sizes, so the call is only modestly better than chance. Stain tone (A pinker, B more purple) and specimen size (A biopsy-sized, B a large resection) differ, and I did not weigh them.

Slide B shows prominent intracellular mucin with focal extracellular mucin, tubulovillous/villiform growth and focal mildly serrated luminal contours. These are the weak population-level correlates of KRAS mutation. Slide A is a high-grade, poorly differentiated, mucin-poor, eosinophilic, pleomorphic carcinoma with dense inflammation, a phenotype more often seen in KRAS/BRAF wild-type MSS tumours. The two cases therefore differ in the direction of the priors, so I call B. These associations are weak per case, so the probability stays modest (p_A = 0.38). Slide A is a much smaller tissue sample than B. Stain tone is similar between the two, with A slightly more eosinophilic. Neither difference was used for the call.

Slide B is a low-grade, villiform/tubulovillous adenocarcinoma with abundant intracellular goblet-cell mucin, which matches the reported weak KRAS tendencies (mucinous differentiation, villous growth, adenoma-like phenotype). Slide A is a high-grade pleomorphic tumour with eosinophilic cytoplasm and a prominent lymphoid response, a phenotype more often linked to MSI/BRAF-type tumours, although both are stated MSS and BRAF-wild-type, so this argues only weakly against KRAS in A. These are population tendencies, not per-case markers. A is a small biopsy-sized specimen and B a large resection, and their stain tones differ; I did not use these differences. Overall this is a weak morphology-based lean towards B.

Slide A has marked mucinous differentiation: extensive extracellular mucin lakes on the overview, plus intracellular mucin and signet-ring-like cells at high power. Slide B has none. Mucinous differentiation is the most consistently reported KRAS association in MSS CRC. That pushes toward A, but A's poorly cohesive, highly pleomorphic, budding phenotype is not specific to KRAS. Slide B's exophytic villous/papillary growth is also a weak KRAS prior, so the evidence partly cancels. On balance the mucinous signal is weighted somewhat higher, giving only a modest lean to A. Stain-tone and sampling differences (two of five B fields are normal mucosa) were not used.

The main differentiator is A's extensive extracellular mucin (mucin lakes visible across the overview and mucoid stroma with discohesive cells at high power), the most frequently reported, albeit weak, association with KRAS mutation in CRC. B instead shows non-mucinous tubulovillous/papillary growth, itself a weak KRAS-associated feature, which partially offsets A's signal. A also has more infiltrative poorly differentiated clusters, which is of uncertain relevance. Neither shows serrated architecture. Overall the evidence is weak and I place only modest probability on A.

Slide A shows extensive extracellular mucin lakes with floating tumour clusters and an infiltrative, budding pattern. Mucinous differentiation is the most often reported, though weak, H&E correlate of KRAS mutation. Slide B is an exophytic, villous-appearing, moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma without mucin. Villous growth is also a weak KRAS prior, so the two signals partly offset each other. The mucin in A could reflect treatment effect rather than a true mucinous phenotype. Slide B had only 2 of 5 high-power fields containing tumour, which limits that comparison. I lean slightly towards A, with low confidence.

Neither slide shows mucinous carcinoma, signet-ring cells or definite serrated architecture, so the evidence is weak. B has more intracellular mucin, more eosinophilic cytoplasm and an exophytic, crowded, partly cribriform/villoglandular growth pattern. These match the weak KRAS-associated tendencies slightly better. A has more tumour budding and dirty necrosis, which may also lean toward KRAS but is closer to conventional moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma. Some of the difference is sampling: B is a superficial, tumour-dense section, while A is a stroma-rich invasive front. That limits how much weight these findings can carry. This is a slight lean toward B, near chance.

The only listed prior that separates the slides is villous/papillary growth: A has a clear exophytic villiform component with eosinophilic columnar cells and equivocal focal serration, while B is a crowded cribriform/solid adenocarcinoma without villous fronds. Mucinous differentiation is mild and roughly equal (intracellular vacuoles in both, no extracellular pools). Budding/clusters are slightly more visible in A, but that probably reflects A containing the invasive front while B is superficial fragmented tissue - a sampling difference, not biology. These are weak population-level tendencies, so the call is barely above chance (p=0.55).

Neither slide shows mucinous, serrated or signet-ring features, so the strongest reported priors are absent from both. B has somewhat more villous/papillary frond architecture and scattered intracytoplasmic mucin vacuoles; A has more budding and poorly differentiated clusters, but A is a full-thickness section with deep invasive front sampled while B is mostly superficial tumour, so the budding difference largely reflects sampling. The weak villous lean toward B is offset by A's budding, and the overall signal is close to nil. Call B with probability only marginally off 0.5.

Neither slide shows mucin pools, signet-ring cells or serrated architecture, so the main literature priors are absent from both. The only morphologic difference that bears on the priors is A's villous/papillary surface component, a weak population-level association with KRAS; B looks more solid and trabecular but is hard to read. B differs strongly from A in tissue quality (crush, chatter, folds) and stain tone, and I gave those differences no weight. The call is close to a guess, with a small tilt toward A from the villous growth.

Slide A shows villous/papillary exophytic growth with tall-columnar adenoma-like epithelium, which is one of the weak reported associations with KRAS mutation; slide B is a solid, poorly glandular, more pleomorphic carcinoma without mucinous, serrated or villous features. Neither slide shows convincing mucinous differentiation or serration, so the call rests on the villous prior alone, which is a weak population tendency. The marked stain/tissue-quality difference (B dark, hypereosinophilic, folded) was disregarded. Probability is only slightly above 0.5.

Slide A shows the weak KRAS-associated features that are visible here: villiform/papillary surface growth and focal goblet-like intracellular mucin in a moderately differentiated intestinal-type adenocarcinoma. Slide B is a solid, poorly gland-forming tumour with dirty necrosis and pleomorphism, and it has no mucinous or villous component. Neither slide shows serration, and neither has extracellular mucin pools. These are population-level tendencies with little per-case value. Slide B's differentiation read is also confounded by thick, folded, darkly stained sections, so I give only a slight lean to A (p=0.6).

Slide A shows a strongly villous/papillary exophytic architecture with abundant goblet-cell mucin and eosinophilic cytoplasm, which matches the weak population-level associations of KRAS mutation (villous growth, mucinous differentiation). Slide B is a conventional tubular/cribriform adenocarcinoma with dirty necrosis and more pleomorphism, which is the typical pattern but carries no specific signal. These are weak tendencies, not per-case markers, so I put only a modest lean toward A. A and B differ markedly in stain tone (A eosin-heavy and pink, B purple); I did not use that difference in the call.

Slide A shows the features weakly linked to KRAS mutation: marked villous/exophytic growth, abundant intracellular goblet-type mucin, and focal serrated luminal contours with eosinophilic cytoplasm. Slide B is a conventional NOS-type adenocarcinoma with dirty necrosis and little mucin, a pattern somewhat more typical of WNT-driven, KRAS-wild-type MSS tumours. These are population-level tendencies, not per-case markers, and A has no extracellular mucin pools, so the signal is weak. The stain-tone difference (A pinker, B more purple) did not enter the call.

Slide A is a villous, mucin-rich (abundant intracellular goblet-type mucin) exophytic tumour with focal serrated luminal contours, whereas B is a conventional NOS adenocarcinoma with dirty necrosis and minimal mucin, the typical pattern of the canonical/WNT-driven type. Villous growth and mucinous differentiation are the reported weak KRAS associations, so they tilt toward A. These are population tendencies with low per-case reliability, A shows intracellular rather than extracellular mucin (it is not a mucinous carcinoma), and B contributed only 4 tumour fields, so confidence is modest. Stain tone differs (A pinker, B more purple), but it was not used.

The two tumours differ sharply. A is conventional moderately differentiated gland-forming adenocarcinoma with villiform/papillary fronds. B is poorly differentiated and discohesive, with a possible mucoid/signet-ring component, infiltrating muscularis. Villous/papillary growth in A is a weak KRAS-positive prior. Poorly cohesive or signet-ring morphology in MSS, BRAF-wt tumours is, if anything, somewhat less often KRAS-mutant. However, any mucinous component in B would argue the other way, so these priors largely offset. B's focus blur limits assessment. The lean toward A is weak and near chance.

Slide B is largely non-evaluable owing to severe freezing/crush artefact and possibly sampling of muscularis rather than tumour, so a feature-by-feature comparison is not possible. Slide A is a conventional moderately differentiated intestinal-type adenocarcinoma with focal villiform fronds but no mucin or serration, which is at most a very weak KRAS prior. Neither slide shows mucinous or serrated features. The slight lean to A rests on focal villous growth and is close to a guess; the tissue-quality and stain differences carry no KRAS information and were not used.

Slide A shows villiform/papillary gland growth, a weak population-level association with KRAS mutation, and this is the only listed feature present in either slide. Slide B cannot be scored reliably: it is out of focus and degraded, and its fields appear to come from deep infiltrative tumour in muscle with no gland formation. The two slides therefore differ mainly in sampling and quality, which carry no KRAS information. The slight lean to A rests only on A's villous growth and on the absence of any assessable KRAS-associated feature in B. The evidence is very weak, so p stays close to 0.5.
